text:
B: Hello? Is it on?
A: Hiya. Yeah, I think so. I can see you.
B: Right. Good. Darren. Not done one of these before.
A: Me neither. I'm Bethany. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous.
B: You're alright. It's only three minutes, love. Where are you, then?
A: Pontefract.
B: Pontefract? Give over. I'm Castleford. Born in Pontefract hospital, actually.
A: Oh, no way. That's... that's mad, that. I worked in Castleford, at a flower shop. On the main road down near the precinct.
B: Not the one that shut? Little independent place?
A: Yeah. That one. About eighteen month ago now.
B: I knew it. I used to drive past it in the van every day. Shame, that. It were a nice shop.
A: It was. It was sort of my place, you know. I've not really found anything since, so I'm just... erm, looking. Sort of.
B: It's hard round here. Everything's shutting. What did you do there, then? Bouquets and that?
A: Yeah, bouquets, weddings, buttonholes. And I did a lot of the sympathy flowers, for funerals. People are upset when they come in, and I didn't mind. I'd just let them talk.
B: Takes a certain kind of person, that. When me mam died, the lass who did the flowers were dead kind. Made a big difference, actually.
A: I'm sorry about your mam.
B: Ah, it's three year ago now. Anyway. What about you, are you married? Sorry, saw the photo.
A: Yeah, I am. My husband's called Craig. He'd like you, I think. He's Cas Tigers mad. I saw your throw in your photo.
B: Ha, did you? Good man. Is he going Sunday?
A: He's on nights this week, so I don't know. I sit with him when he watches it on telly. I don't really understand it.
B: Neither do the refs, half the time. Last week were a disgrace. Sorry, I'm just being a grump.
A: No, that's alright. He says the same thing every week.
B: I'm a joiner, by the way. Housing association. Doors, windows, kitchens, boarding up. All over Wakefield district.
A: Oh, that's handy. Our back door sticks all the time. Mabel, that's our dog, she's a whippet, she's scared of it. She's scared of everything, really. The bin lorry especially.
B: Is that her on the settee in the back?
A: Yeah, that's her. She just sleeps all day.
B: Lucky her. Your door'll be the frame dropping. Probably the hinges, nine times out of ten. Easy fix.
A: Really? Craig keeps saying he'll look at it.
B: They all say that. I've been saying I'll do me own guttering since October.
A: Ha. I do little pressed flowers, framed ones, for people. I could swap you one for...
